title: Product-Key Mirror address lookup
hypothesis: On a 256-map additive Cartesian task bank with held-out pair compositions, a factorized Mirror address will recover each composition from shared left/right factors while saving actual bytes versus Product-Key and flat independent maps.
physical_object: shared 8x4 linear map basis with left/right factor tables and optional interaction state
mirror_coordinate: two categorical 4-bit subaddresses selecting one of 16x16 logical combinations
logical_multiplicity: 256 selected linear maps whose quality and functional distinctness are directly measured

development.selection_metric: held-out map nMSE, address accuracy, collision rate, distinct functions, actual bytes, query MACs

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: Both dev worlds: address accuracy >=0.99, held-out nMSE <=1e-6, 256 distinct realized functions, Mirror payload >=10% below Product-Key and flat-table controls, routing MACs <= Product-Key; direct coefficient control >=10% larger for Mirror-specific result.
failure_gate: Any quality or distinct-function gate missed; storage saving <10%; direct control within 10%; or routing compute >1.10x Product Key. Fresh remains sealed.
amendment: The initial invalid development implementation gave the factorized Mirror and direct controls a full 256-entry interaction tensor, and scored held-out functions against maps stored in that tensor. This made the zero error tautological and the storage comparison unfair. Before any fresh access, amend the task to an exactly additive factorized bank with zero interaction, train factor recovery on 192 seen pairs, and evaluate held-out compositions using only recovered left/right factors. Product Key retains a charged 256-value table; independent/flat controls retain full matrices. Fresh seeds remain sealed.
boundaries: post-fit oracle synthetic linear-map mechanism screen
combinatorial address count is not treated as capacity
no end-to-end trained router or LM evidence
